blockers.description: S1 weekly/monthly fix (js/domain/scoring.js, tests/unit/scoring.test.js) is verified by unit tests but user reported it still showed <100% live in the app after the fix landed in the working tree. Most likely cause: score_snapshots rows are precomputed/cached (views never recompute live) and were written by the OLD buggy formula, so a 'Recompute Scores' run in Settings is needed before the corrected values show up. User said 'I'll check the live app first' and has not yet reported back the result.
blockers.workaround: User needs to: (1) hard-refresh / ensure latest JS is loaded (service worker uses stale-while-revalidate for /js/, so a first reload after a source change can still serve stale cached JS), (2) go to Settings > Recompute Scores to rebuild score_snapshots with the corrected formula, (3) re-check the weekly habit's S1 score, (4) report back confirmed/still-wrong so the debug session can be committed and closed, or reopened if still broken.

decisions.decision: S1 grace period explains the 'Woda: wypicie 2 litrów' habit not showing a score — not a bug.
decisions.rationale: data/habits-import-2026-09-17.json shows this habit has startDate 2026-09-14 and only 3 log rows (09-14/15/16); scoring.js's documented 7-day grace period (habits < 7 days old return null scores) is working as designed. It's a Wave 6 habit that only recently went active as part of the phased wave rollout. It will start scoring around 2026-09-21.

decisions.decision: Waveboard heat-map week range changed from hardcoded last-12-weeks to full history from the earliest score_snapshots row, with horizontal scroll and a sticky habit-name column.
decisions.rationale: score_snapshots are written from habit.createdAt to today (not capped at 70 days) except when createdAt is missing, so full-history display is architecturally supported; the 12-week cap was purely a UI limitation.

decisions.decision: Wave-header row in the waveboard now uses a scoped selector (.waveboard-grid .analytics-wave-header td) for sticky positioning, rather than styling the shared bare .analytics-wave-header td class.
decisions.rationale: That class is also used by the plain, non-scrolling desktop analytics table (js/views/desktop/analytics.js); a bare rule would have leaked sticky positioning into a table that never scrolls.
